$comment: Machine-readable delivery status for every requirement ID in
docs/functional-requirements.md, in spec order. Read by tools/fleet to decide
what to queue next. It is a work list, not a source of truth: docs/spec.md and
the README are, and where this file disagrees with one, this file is wrong.
A bare "partial" is rejected: the remaining line is the only part a later pass
cannot work out by reading the repo.
One line per ID, and every ID is always present, so landing a requirement is a
single-line edit rather than an insert - two branches changing different IDs do

API-001.remaining: wire POST /upgrade and POST /drill once their core operations land (UPGR-*, DRIL-*); POST /init, POST /up, POST /import, POST /backup, POST /restore, POST /promote, and GET /status are wired

XCUT-001.remaining: The keystore file driver and local blob adapter now reject relative config.path (a real gap: it was baked into the manifest at init and silently re-resolved against whatever directory a later command ran from). TestUpSucceedsFromBundleCopiedToAnotherDirectory, TestBackupSucceedsFromBundleCopiedToAnotherDirectory (internal/core/backup), TestRestoreSucceedsFromBundleCopiedToAnotherDirectory (internal/core/restore), and now TestPromoteSucceedsFromBundleCopiedToAnotherDirectory (internal/core/promote) prove `up`, `backup`, `restore`, and `promote` all succeed from a bundle physically relocated after the directory it was saved to no longer exists: the keystore driver, blob adapter, and age identity each resolves from a loaded bundle all work after the bundle directory itself is moved. That covers every operation landed so far that consumes a loaded bundle (init, up, status, backup, restore, promote; import addresses instances directly and never touches a bundle). upgrade and drill still need the same proof once each lands (UPGR-*, DRIL-* still open).
